maps.title: The Shrine Road
maps.final_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: illustrated fantasy campaign map background for Breachline. Create one complete full-bleed landscape PNG, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, 3:2.
Traditional oil and acrylic fantasy painting, rich but economical visible brushwork, sophisticated color and atmosphere. VERY HIGH steep three-quarter bird's-eye view of a believable broad stretch of country. No horizon and no sky band. This must read as a navigable regional MAP. Consistent geographic scale throughout: forests are continuous finely textured canopy masses with tiny trees, settlements and buildings occupy credible small footprints. NEVER oversized pictorial tree or building map symbols, no toy diorama. This is a new independent region; do not copy any previous map. Natural terrain rhythm, landforms and waterways make physical sense.
COMPOSITION IS FUNCTIONAL: coordinates below are percentages (x across from LEFT, y down from TOP). At each of the six stated stop coordinates reserve subdued midtone low-detail ground about 8% of width by 12% of height for a future UI marker and label. No visible box or artificial clearing outline. Paint each distinctive landmark IMMEDIATELY ABOVE its coordinate, its approach/foot at the point; location tolerance about 3%. Six landmarks need distinct silhouettes and breathing room even at 340-pixel viewing width. The brief's coordinates are layout instructions only and MUST NOT be printed.
Paint one continuous believable narrow worn physical road/trail from the stated start through all six stop coordinates IN ORDER, conforming to terrain, crossing streams and gorges physically. Route should be easily followable, including in the quiet areas, but should be an ordinary earth/paving road integrated into land, never a highlighted game path or an unrealistically huge highway. No shortcuts bypassing a stop. A few secondary traces can be subordinate. Put detail at the landmarks and simplify terrain between, with a few large coherent value shapes. All architecture, bridges, stairs, sluices must visibly connect, with abutments and roads on BOTH ends. The landscape fills every edge; no parchment, tabletop, frame, or decorative cartography.
Absolutely NO text, letters, words, numbers, titles, labels, pins, circles, seals, dots, compass, arrows, dashed lines, glowing/highlighted routes, UI, political borders, emblems, logos or watermarks. No battle, gore, corpses, gold scars/threads, gods, apocalyptic effects. No photograph, satellite imagery, 3D render, vector map, game screenshot, anime. No oversized creatures. Tiny people only when purposeful; do not insert cosmopolitan fantasy crowds.

VIGIL — western river basin ascending to mountain foothills. Clear warm MORNING light; green-gold grassland, ivory rock, cool sky-blue water and shadow. No red cloth. A humble pilgrimage from inhabited country to one almost impossibly modest shrine. Predominantly land; a river descends from top to bottom on the left, mountains rise toward upper right.
Road: enter at (4,95), run to (16,74), east-southeast into (41,83), ascend northeast to (56,53), then northwest to (31,34), turn northeast across (61,23), finally east-northeast to (86,17). One continuous winding route; do not substitute a direct road to the shrine.
Six landmarks, immediately ABOVE each coordinate:
1 (16,74): broad shallow ford across the left-side river, connected road visibly approaching both banks. A few tiny russet-earth raider tents and picketed pack animals on the near bank. No grand bridge.
2 (41,83): dark guarded forest canopy, deliberately overgrown old paving and a few felled trunks blocking it; road threads through but remains traceable. Forest is a dense canopy patch of thousands of correctly scaled trees, not a handful of giant tree icons.
3 (56,53): a narrow traversable pass between TWO distinct rocky shoulders, with a tiny rough cairn and watch fire on the saddle. Path naturally climbs, clears the saddle, and leaves to northwest.
4 (31,34): a solitary old imperial stone gate standing with NO enclosing walls, weathered, larger than the nearby little tents yet very small relative to this region. Subtle scholar lamps and surveying equipment around its feet, quiet forecourt below for marker.
5 (61,23): a broad pale fallow meadow on a high shelf, untouched grass with low rounded mounds, no furrows, no bones and no people. Its uncanny stillness comes from an uninterrupted pale shape; route skirts through its lower part.
6 (86,17): one tiny stone room with a single dark doorway on a bare height, reached by a long narrow worn stair connected to the approaching path. It must be the SMALLEST and most humble building, not a temple, dome, tower or palace. No glow or visible flame. Stair foot at the coordinate and little shrine directly above.
Landmarks at least 5% from the edges; the shrine sits safely inside the frame. Realistic architectural scale, expansive intervening land, softly sunlit open terrain to support later labels.

GNOSIS — eastern coastal region, sea on RIGHT, increasingly old upland country to LEFT. DRY DUSK; deep blue and teal, brass/amber lamps beginning to shine in inhabited areas. Readable rich twilight, no rain, no murky darkness. Theme: practical human invention and its consequences, ending at the remains of an engineering ability no longer understood.
Road starts in harbour at right edge (97,86), through (86,76), northwest to (62,62), southwest to (38,74), northwest to (17,52), northeast to (40,30), then northwest to (16,15). Continuous road with physically sensible gradients, spans and intersections.
Six landmarks immediately ABOVE those marker coordinates:
1 (86,76): compact slate-roof harbour city cut by a few canals, modest brass-topped lamp tower as its silhouette, connected quays and small boats. Town seen as many tiny roof masses, not a giant city icon. All bridges connect built banks, no stairs ending in water.
2 (62,62): working sluices and a stepped reservoir that feeds a long, supported aqueduct stretching through part of this landscape; tiny workers and one small brass helper repair a channel. Functional, cared-for construction, not a huge fantasy machine. All water conveyance connections make physical sense.
3 (38,74): terraced hill farms and scattered houses with small irrigation channels. Tiny carts halted at a junction imply a disagreement. Rural footprint spread across the slopes, visually different from harbour and waterworks.
4 (17,52): small disciplined pale roadside fort with ivory and restrained gold accents. Its gate controls this road's entry into high country; show the route passing under the gate and continuing behind. Not a large city or castle.
5 (40,30): massive EMPTY Old Empire canal cut in a straight line through high dry land, broken lock gate, tiny surveyors down in its bed for scale. Large enough to dwarf modern works, but embedded in continuous terrain; road traverses the dry bed by a believable ramp or intact small bridge. No flowing water in this ancient canal.
6 (16,15): plateau-top old observatory with a great OPEN DOME and one long tilted instrument within, unlit and pointed at nothing visible. Small amber-lamp camp alongside; no beam or mystical effect. The plateau and approach are connected; a clearly navigable path ends at its foot.
Make the upper-right sea an open quiet teal distance. Omit the optional Dawnsail because this image prioritizes route clarity. No extra creatures. Place architecture just above marker footprints, with muted quiet midtone ground below. Use tiny predominantly human workers only, no mixed-species crowds. The proposed city and all terrain are a fresh design, not a reuse of any earlier Ambrel map or rejected atlas.

DOMINION — cold northern moorland, ash grey, bone pale stone, tarnished silver, deep violet heather and lichen. Even cold OVERCAST illumination, clear readable values, subtle beautiful color. Oppressive harsh order closing in, tribute and confinement, NOT a benign tidy utopia. No Gothic castles, skull decor, fangs, gore, overt monsters or explosive darkness. Feel uncomfortable through severe controlled enclosure, stripped land and heavy architecture.
Composition: one CLOCKWISE INWARD SPIRAL ROAD. Start at bottom left (3,94), to (12,80), across lower edge to (50,88), east to (87,68), up right side to (78,24), west across top to (34,18), then turn down and inward to a central black lake and its island court at (50,50). Keep the whole spiral legible; do NOT create a shortcut cutting across the lake. Distinct terrain along each arc.
Six landmarks immediately above stops:
1 (12,80): small cramped living tithe village, smoke from a few chimneys, tiny carts compelled into a straight queue beside a severe pale counting house. Humble soot-stained homes, fenced collection yards, no welcoming festival, prosperous sprawl or friendly plaza.
2 (50,88): wide field of low rounded burial barrows in measured rows. A few tiny hooded figures carrying a covered burden carefully between them, no visible bones or corpses. Barrows above coordinate, quiet low-detail road below. Keep minimum 5% edge clearance.
3 (87,68): straight raised salt causeway across a broad pale marsh along the eastern outer curve. Evenly spaced small posts, both ends clearly joined to the main road. Muted midtone stop ground, don't put the UI point over glaring white salt.
4 (78,24): rows of bare pale pruned trees, all actual small trees at consistent landscape scale, one near-invisible gardener. It is subtly uncertain whether they are living trees, but no literal bones. Bleached orchard geometry contrasts with heather outside.
5 (34,18): a silent severe town, constrained rectilinear streets, shuttered windows, NO chimney smoke and NO visible inhabitants. In contrast to the living village, it is emptied, oppressive and forbidding, not attractive civic benevolence. Small continuous roof blocks, no oversized building symbols.
6 (50,50): low WIDE severe pale-stone palace on a small island in a perfectly still BLACK LAKE at centre. Heavy horizontal architecture, blank facades and restricted entries, not a fairytale castle. One narrow physically continuous stone bridge reaches from the incoming road on upper-left shore to a quiet forecourt at the marker point; palace immediately ABOVE that forecourt. Lake surrounds the island, bridge visibly touches shore and island with proper abutments; no disconnected segments. Center position is important.
Scale: many acres between stops; structures and trees tiny relative to terrain, architectural clusters differentiated through silhouettes. Terrain around the spiral spare and progressively less inhabited, with no pictorial map symbols.

FERVOR — huge dry southern interior and red foothills, HOT OPEN country in low LATE-AFTERNOON SUN with long shadows. Ember orange, iron, soot, dry ochre; small contained campfires dotted sparingly. No lava, volcano, apocalyptic sky, no sky band. Restless free bands moving toward a newcomer's attempt to establish a throne. The region feels expansive and alive, with scattered small camps, not a wasteland apocalypse.
Continuous main trail: start upper-left (3,6), descend to (14,22), sweep east-northeast to (44,15), southeast to (76,27), turn southwest to (52,50), then west-southwest to (22,62), finally take a lower sweeping east-southeast arc to (70,80). Do not shortcut the toll station. Road adapts to dry terrain and rock. Minor camp tracks secondary.
Six landmarks immediately ABOVE coordinate:
1 (14,22): small ring of russet tents and plain banners surrounding an open gathering ground, tiny local band holding a vote around ONE small fire, no parade or charging army. Spatially compact encampment, not an enormous arena.
2 (44,15): long line of tiny wagons, pack animals and awnings drawn up on a DRY river crossing, portable market which could leave by morning. Distinguish market's linear silhouette from circular moot. Tiny figures and vehicles naturally scaled.
3 (76,27): broad bright pale salt pan with a small WORKING camp on its near edge and loaded carts. Brightest landform, but keep the actual stop point and label ground just below it an ordinary subdued earth midtone.
4 (52,50): deep winding RED ROCK GORGE, a believable narrow rope bridge joins BOTH rims exactly where the trail crosses. Visible anchor points, bridge deck, matching trail approaches, no disconnected bridge. Tiny lone giant carrying a load along the far rim; moderately larger than nearby humanoids, not a monumental colossus. Gargantuan landform makes scale clear.
5 (22,62): an orderly stone toll station and short wall block a gap in hills. Queue of small carts at its gate. The road visibly enters the gate and continues on the other side, then sweeps toward the final hill, not under mountains.
6 (70,80): naturally stepped hill with a very small ANCIENT STONE SEAT standing alone at the summit, open to the sky; fresh ring of tents and scaffolding at its base imply someone's claim. This is emphatically NOT a castle, temple, grand palace, giant statue or throne sculpted into a mountain. The road reaches a quiet forecourt at the coordinate and a narrow climbing path/stair leads to the top immediately above.
Consistent landscape scale, tiny camps and a few purposeful people only. Avoid a demographic or multi-species sampler. Big broad regions of quiet sunlit ground and restrained brushwork between crisp landmark silhouettes.

GENESIS — deep eastern forests following ONE GREAT INLAND RIVER flowing from upper right to lower left, NOT coast or islands. Widely varied deep greens, moss, bark brown and amber, dappled moving-cloud DAYLIGHT, pools of sun across forest. Large natural forest canopy masses at credible scale, not giant pictorial trees. Nature is varied and active, interrupted by recent industry, ending at an Old Empire city reclaimed by vegetation.
The main river starts near (95,4), flows past the spring at (84,16), through fen at (58,24), bends southeast toward the herd ford at (70,52), then curves west/south to reservoir and dam near (48,70), continues below dam as a much reduced trickle southwest past the old city at (16,72) and exits bottom left. Make drainage and dam hydraulics physically coherent.
Main continuous land trail: start top-right (97,6), to (84,16), west to (58,24), southeast to (70,52), northwest to (42,46), south to (48,76), then west to (16,72). It follows riverbanks where natural, with dry-land detours to the logging strip and city. It must connect through all six points; do not turn it into a separate river or a direct shortcut to the city. Provide physical crossings wherever needed. The trail after dam follows the low downstream bank toward the inland ruined city.
Six landmarks immediately ABOVE coordinates:
1 (84,16): venerable old grove around a clear small spring, distinguishable through several ancient crowns within the continuous canopy. Actual trees remain naturally scaled, not map symbols. One tiny alderkin living tree person and one tiny person planting together: minor purposeful activity, not a repeated water-infrastructure worker scene.
2 (58,24): wide fen threaded with connected channels, low reed paths, tiny flat boats and one or two tiny long-bodied reedcrown grazers in shallow water, with branching reedlike back crests. Wetland a contrasting open textured mass among woodland, not an ocean.
3 (70,52): broad grassy opening with a small herd of large but credible roughly elephant-sized beasts fording the river at shallow water, a few minuscule people watch from the bank. Not colossal creatures. River banks and trail ford visibly connect. No fantasy dinosaur spectacle.
4 (42,46): hard straight STRIP OF STUMPS through forest, a modest logging camp, stacked timber and new road. The clear straight geometry is the primary visual exception to organic canopy, without making the whole forest into a grid.
5 (48,76): new brass-and-stone dam situated immediately above marker, physically spans the whole channel between solid banks. Deep still reservoir unmistakably UPSTREAM above the dam; thin stream DOWNSTREAM below it. Connected maintenance path crosses or skirts the dam and leads onto quiet downstream marker ground. The engineering is striking and capable but clearly an intrusive barrier in the woodland, not a magical mega-wall.
6 (16,72): EXTENSIVE ruined inland Old Empire city spread into the left/lower-left forest, great stone halls split by mature roots, roofless interiors full of green. Broad footprint of many naturally small ruined blocks, not one oversized landmark building. Mixed vegetation: moss, ferns, saplings, canopy trees, grasses, varied growth rather than uniform ivy. Not flooded, not in sea. Main recognizable roofless hall just ABOVE marker; quiet overgrown street court at its foot for the future marker.
No Stonehorn, Opaline Kin, giant beasts or crowds. Soft textured forest canopies with selective edges, coherent open river and meadow shapes, no flat green fill, six individually legible landmarks.
